Brown Friday: How to Avoid a Post-Thanksgiving Plumbing Nightmare

Published on November 5, 2024April 12, 2025

Thanksgiving in Greenville, SC, is all about family, food, and cherished traditions. But while many residents are enjoying turkey and pumpkin pie, a different tradition unfolds the day after: “Brown Friday.” Known in the plumbing industry as the busiest day of the year, Brown Friday sees a surge in service calls for clogged drains, broken garbage disposals, and overflowing toilets. While holiday shoppers are out hunting for Black Friday deals, Carolina Heating Service’s plumbing team is busy addressing urgent calls to keep kitchens and bathrooms running smoothly. So, why is Brown Friday such a notorious day for plumbers, and what can you do to avoid an emergency? Let’s dive into why Brown Friday happens and how to safeguard your home’s plumbing during the holiday season.

What’s Behind the Name “Brown Friday”?

The name “Brown Friday” might sound comical, but for plumbers, it’s no laughing matter. The term accurately reflects the post-Thanksgiving spike in service calls. Thanksgiving celebrations put intense pressure on household plumbing as families prepare large meals and host guests. Data from plumbing service platforms like ServiceTitan show that service calls for clogged drains, broken garbage disposals, and mainline stoppages can increase by over 50% on Brown Friday. Carolina Heating Service in Greenville has seen firsthand how holiday gatherings can strain plumbing systems.

The combination of excessive food waste, fats and oils poured down drains, and the increased use of toilets all contribute to this post-holiday plumbing crunch. As a result, Brown Friday is one of the most challenging days of the year for both homeowners and plumbing professionals.

Why Does Thanksgiving Cause Plumbing Problems?

Thanksgiving is one of the busiest days for kitchen and bathroom use, which can lead to various plumbing problems. Here’s why plumbing issues tend to surge during this holiday:

  1. Overloaded Garbage Disposals: While garbage disposals are convenient, they have their limits. Items like bones, fibrous vegetables, and grease can jam the disposal, dull blades, or cause the motor to overheat and stop working.
  2. Clogged Kitchen Drains: Foods common to Thanksgiving meals, such as potato peels, gravy, and cooking oils, can stick to the inside of pipes. Once they cool, they solidify and create blockages that restrict water flow.
  3. Overused Toilets: Holiday gatherings mean more people using the facilities. Toilets that are flushed frequently, especially with non-flushable items, can lead to clogs and backups.

Plumbing Data and Trends

The reputation of Brown Friday is supported by real data. Reports from platforms like ServiceTitan show significant spikes in service calls for mainline stoppages, garbage disposal issues, and drain cleanings right after Thanksgiving. Some plumbers report up to a 20% increase in service requests compared to an average day. This pattern underscores the strain that Thanksgiving activities place on household plumbing systems. While “Brown Friday” may sound humorous, dealing with plumbing problems during a holiday weekend is anything but fun.

Tips to Avoid Brown Friday Plumbing Issues

To avoid a post-Thanksgiving plumbing emergency, follow these simple but effective tips to protect your Greenville home’s plumbing:

1. Limit What Goes Down the Garbage Disposal

Only certain types of food waste should go down the disposal. Avoid fibrous foods, grease, and bones. When using the disposal, run cold water to help flush food particles through the system effectively.

2. Dispose of Grease Correctly

A major mistake is pouring grease down the drain. Although liquid when hot, grease hardens as it cools, causing clogs. Pour grease into a container, let it solidify, and dispose of it in the trash.

3. Use Drain Screens

Drain screens are simple but effective at catching food scraps and preventing clogs. Use them in your kitchen and bathroom sinks to keep unwanted particles out of the pipes.

4. Stagger Appliance Use

Running the dishwasher, laundry machine, and taking showers at the same time can overburden your plumbing. Space out these tasks to reduce pressure and prevent backups.

5. Share Bathroom Etiquette

It may feel a bit awkward, but a reminder to guests to only flush toilet paper can go a long way. Items labeled “flushable” aren’t always safe for plumbing. Place a small sign or have a trash bin available to keep pipes clear.

Preparing for a Smooth Thanksgiving

Brown Friday may be a well-known day for plumbers, but with a few smart precautions, you can avoid the stress of an emergency service call. By being mindful of what goes down the drain, disposing of grease properly, and spacing out appliance use, you can keep your plumbing in top shape. If an issue does arise, know that Carolina Heating Service is ready to assist Greenville homeowners with quick, professional plumbing services. Enjoy your Thanksgiving with peace of mind, knowing we’re here to help. From all of us at Carolina Heating Service, happy Thanksgiving!
